description: Indiana-only rules checked against the 2026 Indiana Code and Indiana BMV pages. National rules stay in the baseline. No fines.

questions.q: Indiana's maximum speed in an urban district, unless a special hazard or an authorized lower limit applies, is
questions.explanation: IC 9-21-5-2(a)(1) sets 30 mph in an urban district.

questions.q: The maximum speed Indiana sets for an alley is
questions.explanation: IC 9-21-5-2(a)(8) sets 15 mph in an alley. A local authority may later alter an alley limit, but the statutory alley maximum is 15.

questions.q: On an Indiana interstate outside an urbanized area of at least 50,000 people, the maximum for a vehicle that is not a heavy truck under the truck rule is
questions.explanation: IC 9-21-5-2(a)(3) sets 70 mph on a national interstate or defense highway outside an urbanized area of at least 50,000. Subdivision (4) lowers that to 65 for a vehicle other than a bus with a declared gross weight over 26,000 pounds.

questions.q: Indiana's statutory maximum on Interstate 465 is
options: 70 mph, the same as a rural interstate
questions.explanation: IC 9-21-5-2(a)(9) sets 65 mph on Interstate Highway 465. The general rural-interstate figure of 70 does not replace that subdivision.

questions.q: Indiana's under-21 offense in IC 9-30-5-8.5 applies when a driver under 21 operates a vehicle with an alcohol concentration equivalent of
options: At least 0.02 but less than 0.08 gram
At least 0.04 gram, the commercial figure
questions.explanation: IC 9-30-5-8.5 makes that 0.02-but-less-than-0.08 range a Class C infraction for a person under 21. A result of 0.08 or more is charged under IC 9-30-5-1 instead. The code section does not use a zero-tolerance 'any amount' rule. At least 0.02 gram but less than 0.08 gram per 100 milliliters of blood or 210 liters of breath.

questions.q: An Indiana driver under 21 who is convicted of two or more traffic offenses must
options: Complete a Driver Safety Program within 90 days or be suspended
Automatically lose the license for one year at the second conviction
Wait until 12 points accumulate before any program is required
Receive a 4-point credit without taking a course
questions.explanation: The BMV Driver Safety Program page says a driver under 21 is required to complete a BMV-approved program after two or more traffic-offense convictions. Once the BMV is notified, the course must be finished within 90 days or driving privileges will be suspended.

questions.q: For an Indiana driver who is not in the under-21 mandatory class, two or more traffic-offense convictions within 12 months
options: Always suspend the license for 6 months with no course option
May require a BMV-approved Driver Safety Program
Do not matter until the driver reaches 30 points
questions.explanation: The same BMV page says state law provides that persons convicted of two or more traffic offenses within a 12-month period may be required to complete a BMV-approved Driver Safety Program. That sentence is 'may,' not an automatic suspension.

questions.q: Successful completion of a BMV-approved Driver Safety Program
options: Removes every conviction from the driving record
Applies a 4-point credit that may be used only once every three years
Applies a 4-point credit every year the driver asks for it
questions.explanation: The BMV page says completion applies a 4-point credit to the Indiana official driver record. The credit may be applied only once every three years. Another completed course extends that credit period for three years from the new completion date.

questions.q: An Indiana learner's permit may be issued at 15 only if the applicant
options: Has already held a license in another state for one year
Is enrolled in an approved behind-the-wheel course
Finishes 50 hours of practice before the knowledge exam
questions.explanation: The BMV learner's-permit page says a permit is available at 15 to someone enrolled in an approved behind-the-wheel course who presents a valid certificate of driver education, identification, and who passes vision and knowledge exams. Without driver education, the same page sets the permit age at 16.

questions.q: An Indiana probationary driver's license requires 180 days on a learner's permit and
options: Age 16 with driver education, or 16 and 270 days without
Age 15 with or without driver education
Age 16 and 90 days if the driving log is finished
questions.explanation: The BMV probationary-license page requires a learner's permit held for 180 days, age 16 with successful driver education, or age 16 years and 270 days without that course.

questions.q: In Indiana, what is the youngest age at which you can get a learner's permit for a car?
questions.explanation: Indiana issues a learner's permit for a car at 15 years at the earliest.
questions.remember: Indiana car permit: 15 years at the earliest.

questions.q: In Indiana, how long must a driver under 18 hold a learner's permit before moving to the next license?
questions.explanation: Indiana requires drivers under 18 to hold the learner's permit for 6 months.

provenance.manual: Driver's Licenses, Permits & IDs: Probationary Driver's License

questions.q: How many hours of supervised driving must a teen in Indiana complete before getting a provisional license?
questions.explanation: Indiana requires 50 hours of supervised driving before the provisional license.

provenance.manual: Driver's Licenses, Permits & IDs: Driver's License

questions.q: Of a Indiana teen's required supervised driving hours, how many must be at night?
questions.explanation: Indiana requires at least 10 hours of the supervised driving to be at night.
questions.remember: Indiana: 10 hours of the supervised driving at night.

provenance.manual: Driver's Licenses, Permits & IDs: Driver's License

questions.q: In Indiana, what is the youngest age for a full, unrestricted car license?
questions.explanation: Indiana drivers can hold an unrestricted license at 21 years.

questions.q: What score do you need to pass the Indiana car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: You need 80% to pass the Indiana car knowledge test.

provenance.manual: Driver's Licenses, Permits & IDs: Knowledge Exam

questions.q: In Indiana, how long is the license suspension for an adult's first refusal of a breath or blood test?
questions.explanation: A first refusal in Indiana brings a suspension of 1 year.
questions.remember: Indiana, first refusal: 1 year without a license.

questions.q: What is the highest standard speed limit for cars on rural interstates in Indiana?
questions.explanation: Rural interstates in Indiana can be posted up to 70 mph for cars.
questions.remember: Indiana rural interstate: up to 70 mph.

questions.q: Which best describes Indiana's law on drivers using a phone?
options: No statewide ban on phone use or texting
Only texting is banned for all drivers
Phone use is banned only for new or young drivers
Hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers
questions.explanation: Indiana: hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers.

questions.q: When is a left turn on a red light allowed in Indiana?
options: From a one-way or two-way street onto a one-way street
Only from a one-way street onto a one-way street
questions.explanation: In Indiana, a left turn on red (after a full stop, where not prohibited) is allowed: only from a one-way street onto a one-way street.
questions.remember: Indiana left on red: one-way onto one-way only.

questions.q: How is Indiana's seat belt law for adults enforced?
options: Primary: police can stop you just for not wearing a seat belt
Secondary: police can cite you only after stopping you for something else
No seat belt law for adults
questions.explanation: Indiana seat belt enforcement is primary.

provenance.manual: What is the Indiana law concerning seat belts? – IN.gov

questions.q: Until what age must a child ride in a car seat or booster seat in Indiana?
questions.explanation: Indiana requires a car seat or booster until 8 years, with height or weight exceptions.
questions.remember: Indiana: car or booster seat until 8 years.

questions.q: What is Indiana's minimum liability insurance (injury per person / injury per crash / property damage)?
questions.explanation: Indiana requires at least $25,000 / $50,000 / $25,000.
